title: CP 321 - Disability, Long-Term Care, and Long-Duration Health Contracts

topics.title: Plan and Product Provisions
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to describe benefits typically offered under long duration contracts (disability income, long term care, critical illness, Medicare Supplement).

outcomes.text: Describe typical organizations offering these contracts and their motivation for offering each type
Describe each type of contract listed above
Evaluate the potential moral hazards and financial and legal risks associated with each contract
Describe Social Security disability income benefits in the United States

topics.title: Manual Rates
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to calculate rates for each of the contracts described in Learning Objective 1.

outcomes.text: Identify and evaluate sources of data needed for pricing, including the quality, appropriateness, and limitations of each data source
Calculate and recommend assumptions
Calculate and recommend a manual rate (includes base rate development and applying a rating manual) and describe the role of data credibility used to calculate the rate
Identify critical metrics to evaluate actual vs. expected results
Recommend strategies for properly modelling, pricing, underwriting, and funding case-specific risks
Describe the purpose and objectives of Guaranty Associations and the multi-state framework for long term care rate increases
Apply actuarial best practices in evaluating and projecting cash flows (premiums, claims, investment income, expenses, commissions), liabilities, and required capital

topics.title: Reserving
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to apply valuation principles for long-duration contracts.

outcomes.text: Describe and calculate types of non-claim reserves held for long duration health contracts: policy reserves, unearned premium reserves, and premium deficiency reserves

Describe and calculate types of claim reserves held for long duration health contracts: PVANYD (present value of amounts not yet due), ICOS (in course of settlement), and IBNR (incurred but not reported)
Explain the limitations and biases of traditional valuation methods
Calculate appropriate claim reserves given data
Describe, calculate, and evaluate the impact of environmental factors on reserve calculations (trend, seasonality, claim processing changes, etc.)
Evaluate data resources and appropriateness for calculating reserves
Apply appliable best practices related to reserving

topics.title: Insurer Financial Statements
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to prepare and interpret insurance company financial statements for long duration contracts.

outcomes.text: Compare valuation standards under IFRS 17, US GAAP, and Statutory Accounting
Prepare financial statements in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and IFRS 17
Interpret the results of both statutory and GAAP statements from the viewpoint of stakeholders, including regulators, senior management, and investors
Project financial outcomes and recommend a strategy
Apply applicable best practices

topics.title: Asset Adequacy
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to evaluate asset matching and asset adequacy standards for long duration contracts.

outcomes.text: Understand the principles of Asset-Liability Management (ALM)
Evaluate techniques for addressing mismatched assets and liabilities
Describe asset adequacy approaches commonly applied to long-duration health contracts
Describe cash flow projections and interactions between asset and liability cash flows

topics.title: Retiree Group Benefits
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to design and perform valuations of retiree group benefits.

outcomes.text: Describe why employers offer retiree group benefits
Determine appropriate demographic, economic, and benefit assumptions and apply to a retiree health valuation
Determine employer liabilities, service cost, and expense for post-retirement and post-employment benefits and prepare disclosure information for financial reporting purposes
Describe current issues faced by governments, employers, and employees related to post-retirement and post-employment benefits
Apply actuarial best practices to post-retirement and post-employment benefit plans
Propose ways to manage the range of risks faced by plan participants and retirees through retiree health and life plan designs
Advise a plan sponsor regarding the choice of design elements for their retiree health program given situational context
